title: Tanawpamana: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models on Philippine Cultural Heritage Sites
abstract: arXiv:2610.17596v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-language models are increasingly used to identify and describe places, yet their recognition and knowledge of specific cultures remain poorly understood, particularly in underrepresented regions such as the Philippines. This study introduces the Tanawpamana Dataset, a repository of Philippine heritage site images with metadata based on the Talapamana registry of the National Commission for Culture and the Arts of the Philippines. We also introduce the Tanawpamana Benchmark, comprising 4,046 tasks designed to evaluate models' recognition and knowledge of heritage sites. Evaluating seven vision-language models, we find that they struggle more with fine-grained visual discrimination among similar heritage sites than with coarse recognition, and that their geographic knowledge is weaker when inferred from image inputs than from text.

translated_title: Tanawpamana：在菲律宾文化遗产地上的视觉-语言模型基准测试
translated_abstract: 视觉-语言模型越来越多地被用于识别和描述地点，然而它们对特定文化的识别能力和知识水平仍然鲜为人知，尤其是在菲律宾等代表性不足的地区。本研究推出了Tanawpamana数据集，这是一个菲律宾遗产地图像库，其元数据基于菲律宾国家文化艺术委员会的Talapamana登记册。我们还推出了Tanawpamana基准测试，包含4,046个任务，旨在评估模型对遗产地的识别能力和知识水平。通过对七个视觉-语言模型的评估，我们发现这些模型在相似遗产地之间的细粒度视觉区分上比粗粒度识别更为困难，并且它们从图像输入推断地理知识的能力弱于从文本推断。
tldr: 本研究构建了基于菲律宾文化遗产地的Tanawpamana数据集和包含4046个任务的基准测试，评估发现视觉-语言模型在细粒度区分相似遗产地方面的能力弱于粗粒度识别，且从图像推断地理知识的能力弱于从文本推断。
en_tdlr: This study introduces the Tanawpamana Dataset and Benchmark of 4,046 tasks based on Philippine cultural heritage sites, finding that vision-language models struggle more with fine-grained visual discrimination among similar heritage sites and infer geographic knowledge better from text than from images.
